findings.title: TableWidgetVisualization is rendered with hardcoded empty data when feature flag is on
findings.body: When the `use-table-widget-visualization` feature flag is enabled, the new `TableWidgetVisualization` is rendered with hardcoded `columns={[]}` and `tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}}`. All the real `result.data`, `result.meta`, `fields`, etc. that are passed to the original `StyledSimpleTableChart` are discarded. This means any organization with the flag enabled will see an empty table widget with no rows and no columns. The implementation appears to be an incomplete placeholder; it should pass through `fields`, `result.data`, `result.meta`, and a derived `columns` array rather than constant empty values.

findings.title: Exception handler swallows all errors at info level
findings.body: `get_environment_info` catches bare `Exception` and logs it at `logger.info` (`get_environment_info.no-environment`). Unexpected errors like database failures, N+1 query explosions, or programming errors are silently downgraded to an info-level event with no stack trace, making them invisible in standard error monitoring. Either catch the specific expected exceptions (e.g. `Group.DoesNotExist`) or log at `logger.warning`/`logger.exception` so the failure shows up in Sentry's own error tracking. The current behavior risks hiding real production issues while a comment marks it as `intentional`.

findings.title: Analytics event recorded before feature flag check
findings.body: The `preprod_artifact.api.assemble` analytics event is emitted at the very top of `post()` and runs unconditionally — before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` feature flag check, schema validation, and chunk verification. As a result, every unauthorized or invalid request still generates an analytics record, polluting the metric with traffic that did not actually assemble an artifact and inflating `preprod_artifact.api.assemble` counts. The analytics call should be moved to after the feature flag and validation checks so it only fires for successful/meaningful requests.

findings.title: Unescaped markdown title injection
findings.body: `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` formats issue titles into the markdown template `* ‼️ [**{title}**]({url}){environment}\n` without escaping markdown control characters. A title containing characters like `*`, `_`, `[`, or `]` will be interpreted by markdown renderers and can break the comment formatting (or be used to inject unintended markdown). Consider sanitizing or escaping the title before substituting it into the template.

findings.title: Organization-type actors silently become owner-less
findings.body: `create()` only sets `owner_user_id`/`owner_team_id` when the actor is a user or team. The `ActorField` it depends on accepts organization actors as well; if such an actor is passed, the Detector is silently created with both owner ids set to `None`, giving no error and no diagnostic. Either reject organization actors in validation, or document/encode that organization ownership is not supported. The added tests only cover user and team owners, so this gap isn't caught.

findings.title: Migrations silently no-op; relies on unverified external migration
findings.body: Both 0917 and 0920 were turned into `return`-only no-ops with a comment pointing to `0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py` as the migration that actually performs the data conversion. If 0921 does not exist in the codebase (it is not in the diff for this PR), then on any environment that previously had data in `sentry_savedsearch` with `visibility=ORGANIZATION`, no migration will ever convert those saved searches to `GroupSearchView`. A maintainer should verify that 0921 is present and has run in production before merging, otherwise this PR silently breaks a previously-working data migration.

findings.title: New `equations` parameter added to `run_top_events_timeseries_query` without tests
findings.body: `run_top_events_timeseries_query` now accepts and forwards an `equations` parameter through to `rpc_dataset_common.run_top_events_timeseries_query`, but no test exercises the new parameter. The other files changed in the explore area (`visualizes.tsx`, `aggregateFields.tsx`, etc.) update test fixtures to match the `yAxes -> yAxis` rename but nothing verifies the equations path. Add at least one test covering the equations parameter.

findings.title: Null summary can render in the UI when API returns `success=false` with used feedbacks
findings.body:
`tooFewFeedbacks` is only true when `numFeedbacksUsed === 0 && !data.success`. The `FeedbackSummary` component checks `tooFewFeedbacks` and `isError` to decide whether to render, but it does not check whether `summary` is null. If the API returns `success: false, summary: null, numFeedbacksUsed > 0`, the component renders the title plus an empty `

null

`. Either also bail out when `summary == null`, or have the hook set `tooFewFeedbacks` more conservatively.

findings.title: Empty error_ids returned from snuba can cause validation errors in log assembly
findings.body: `error_ids = response[0].get("error_ids", []) if response else []` assumes `response[0]` exists. In tests where `query_replay_instance` is not set up, the endpoint relies on the integration being mocked. In production, if the snuba call returns no rows (but does return a `[]` array), `response[0]` is `undefined` and the optional chaining would handle that, but then `error_events` is `[]` — fine. However, when `disable_error_fetching` is false and `error_ids` contains ids that no longer resolve in nodestore (a normal race after deletion), the `fetch_error_details` wrapper currently swallows exceptions silently with `sentry_sdk.capture_exception`, but the test `test_get_with_error` does not exercise the empty-error-ids path. Worth adding a regression test for the case where `error_ids` is present but all ids miss in nodestore.

findings.title: Falsy custom cell returns treated as 'no custom renderer'
findings.body: `renderTableBodyCell` is typed as `React.ReactNode | undefined`. The implementation uses `if (cell) { return cell }` to decide whether to fall back to the default renderer, which treats falsy ReactNodes (`0`, `false`, empty string) as 'no custom renderer'. In practice custom renderers typically return JSX or `undefined`, but the contract should use `cell !== undefined` to avoid a future footgun when a renderer intentionally returns `false` to render nothing.

findings.title: Renaming inner parameter `organization` to `org` may obscure the dead-data branch
findings.body: The diff renames the inner parameter in `getCustomFieldRenderer` from `organization?: Organization` to `org?: Organization` to avoid shadowing the prop. The intent is fine, but combined with the fact that the parameter is never actually used (the previous code passed it to `datasetConfig.getCustomFieldRenderer` and the new code still does not), it confirms that this function takes a parameter it never consumes. Recommend dropping the parameter entirely from the signature so callers don't have to pass it.
